extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers interested in home security and popular scientific studies (homeowners, builders, and lay scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting, installing, configuring, and maintaining electric burglar (and related fire) alarm apparatus in private houses and business premises, including component selection, wiring practice, annunciator selection, central monitoring, and cost/maintenance considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Window circuit-closer design (roller spring contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Window attachments are usually simple springs placed in the casing so that the movement of the sash presses them together. One form consists of a roller on the end of a spring arm, which keeps it pressed out from contact with a metal strip, through which the circuit is completed. Placed in the casing, the roller stands out and is received in a pocket in the edge of the sash, so that the motion of the sash brings the roller arm and metal strip into contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use roller-on-spring-arm contacts recessed into sash pockets; elongate pocket in upper sash for ventilation to permit free movement; when lower sash left open, cover a push-pin in sill with obstruction (flower-pot) so removal is necessary for entrance. Devices must be so disposed that a sufficient number properly placed could make intrusion without giving an alarm simply impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wiring concealment and routing
rubrics_metrics.description: The wires forming the circuit are of insulated copper, carefully put up so as to be completely hidden from view. They are run in grooves in the wood-work, carried beneath a floor, or on its face, according to circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceal wiring in grooves, under floors, or otherwise hidden to prevent detection or tampering; properly hidden wires 'once in place, remain unchanged for any period, causing neither trouble nor expense.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Battery selection — Le Clanche battery recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The Le Clanche battery ... is very simple in construction, exhales no noxious gases when in operation, does not waste the material when no current is passing, and needs but very little attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Le Clanche-type cells (positive: gas carbon in porous cell with peroxide of manganese and carbon; negative: amalgamated zinc; electrolyte: sal-ammoniac) assembled (commonly four elements in wooden case). Choose batteries that require little attention and do not emit noxious gases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Night/day circuit configuration and annunciator placement
rubrics_metrics.description: In the daytime, when the doors and windows are open, the circuit is continuous at all points except at the alarm apparatus. At night this is reversed, the circuit being closed at the instrument, and broken at all of the points protected. A movement at any of these points which closes the circuit gives the alarm and turns the proper needle on the annunciator. The alarm apparatus being placed in a sleeping-apartment in a private house, and in the watchman's room in a place of business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annunciator/alarmer should be placed where an occupant or watchman can respond (sleeping-apartment or watchman's room). Arrange wiring so daytime configuration avoids false alarms and nighttime configuration makes any protected-point breach trigger alarm and indicate correct needle on annunciator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual/automatic connection schedule (attendant and clock disconnect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The connection with the alarm is made at night by an attendant, and broken at any desired time in the morning. In private houses fitted with electric bells, a clock is often provided that disconnects the alarm in the morning and turns the current on to a bell placed in the servants' room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide simple manual connection by attendant, or an automatic clock mechanism similar to an alarm-clock to disconnect alarm in morning and switch bell circuits as desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and testing frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: The only case in which there is room for failure of the system is when the battery power is not sufficient to operate the alarm. But it is a very simple matter to provide against this. Tests once every month or two, and the experience soon gained in using the battery, will enable one to know at any time the state of the system. None of the other parts need ever cause any solicitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test battery power monthly or bi-monthly; monitoring battery condition prevents most system failures; other components generally require little maintenance if correctly installed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central-office monitoring with galvanometers for business centers
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet the difficulty of watchmen being overpowered, the plan is sometimes adopted of making the alarm sound in a central office of the company furnishing the apparatus. Each building protected is connected on a closed circuit with the central office, at which place delicate galvanometers are used as indicators. The circuit of each building is independent of all others. Any change in the resistance of any circuit is instantly shown by the deflection of the proper needle, and an alarm started.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent closed circuits per building to central office, employ sensitive galvanometer indicators that detect any resistance change (opening, cutting) instantly. Ensure system resistance includes apparatus resistance so simple line bypass with inserted resistance is impractical; include circuit-breakers judiciously to detect tunneling attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tamper-detection for safes (dual foil-insulated cabinet)
rubrics_metrics.description: The safe is placed in a light wooden cabinet lined with a metallic casing, consisting of two sheets of tin-foil insulated from each other by a thin sheet of non-conducting material. The wires from a battery are connected each with one of the sheets of foil. So delicate is the insulation that the sticking of a pin in the cabinet closes the circuit and deflects the needle, and sounds the alarm in the central office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect safes with dual-foil insulated enclosures wired to alarm so minute penetrations (pin prick) alter circuit and trigger alarm; adopt sufficient sensitivity for valuable stores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annunciator capacity must match number of protected rooms
rubrics_metrics.description: Annunciators range in price from thirty dollars with four indications to one hundred dollars with twenty. The annunciator used should have as many indications as there are rooms protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select annunciator with number of indications equal to number of distinct rooms/points to be protected to allow precise localization of alarm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation unit costs (windows and doors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of circuit-closers, including the placing in position and laying the wire, is three dollars a window when both sashes are connected. The same devices for doors vary from one and a half to two and a half dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget using per-unit cost estimates: ~$3 per window (both sashes), $1.50–$2.50 per door device; total costs depend on annunciator size and number of openings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical coverage and expected total cost
rubrics_metrics.description: In ordinary city houses it is only necessary to connect the windows and doors, front and back, of the first two stories and the opening in the roof. The entire cost will not generally exceed one hundred dollars. In the country the cost would of course be somewhat greater, in the average house probably between a hundred and fifty and two hundred dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For typical city houses protect front/back windows and doors of first two stories plus roof opening; expect total installation cost generally under $100 in city, $150–$200 in country houses; maintenance expense mainly battery upkeep (~$1/year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fire-alarm thermostat design and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The system consists in placing in the ceiling of a room a number of mercury bulbs, which close an electric circuit when the temperature rises above a certain point and set off an alarm. One form of the bulb or thermostat ... The bulbs are usually manufactured to make this contact at a temperature of 120° Fahr. The thermostat is set in a bell-shaped shield of sheet-metal ... They are placed about twenty feet apart in large rooms, a couple being sufficient for those of ordinary size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install mercury-bulb thermostats in ceilings, set to close at ~120°F; space them ≈20 feet apart in large rooms (fewer for ordinary rooms); provide annunciator/central monitoring similar to burglar alarm so building and room location are indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annunciator on building face for central fire signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Each building is provided with an annunciator placed on the front, where it can be readily inspected. The signal given at the office indicates the building, and the annunciator on the face of the building gives the room in which the fire is located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mount external annunciator on building facade to show room location when central office receives alarm, facilitating external inspection and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Battery as primary point of system vulnerability
rubrics_metrics.description: The only case in which there is room for failure of the system is when the battery power is not sufficient to operate the alarm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat battery capacity/health as critical; implement regular tests and simple preventive maintenance to ensure adequate power at all times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of annunciator/alarms to deter burglars (psychological protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Valuable as is the protection in any particular case of attempted robbery, the general immunity from such attempts that the presence of the apparatus secures is of still greater moment. Burglars will not generally take such risks as those imposed by an efficient alarm system, and will therefore give a house so protected a wide berth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that visible presence of alarm apparatus provides deterrent value in addition to functional detection; consider making presence known to discourage attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concealed circuit detection via interior circuit-closers
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the wires be cut, buttons under the carpet or circuit-closers in interior doors will reveal the burglar's presence in perhaps every case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment perimeter wiring with interior circuit-closers (under-carpet buttons, interior door closers) to detect intruders even when external lines are severed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of mental imagery via questionnaires and graded scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: I draw my conclusions from ... a long list of questions which I circulated, besides obtaining batches of replies to the same questions from various schools. The answers ... I take a haphazard bundle of returns, mark them as an examiner would mark the papers of candidates, sort them in the order of their marks, and clip them into a portfolio. If I open the book in the middle I read the medium value; ... at one quarter from the beginning I read the highest quartile value ... one eighth ... an octile value; one sixteenth ... a sub-octile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess visualizing faculty with standardized questionnaires, score responses, and use rank-order sorting to derive quartiles/octiles/sub-octiles to characterize population distribution of imagery vividness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary metric: vividness of mental imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: There are great differences in the power of forming pictures of objects in the mind's eye; in some persons the faculty ... is so feeble that they hardly visualize at all, ... Other persons perceive past scenes with a distinctness and an appearance of reality that differ little from actual vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate subjects on vividness continuum from almost none to near-actual vision; use vividness as a principal dimension when evaluating visualizing ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary metric: completeness / scope of image
rubrics_metrics.description: The part of the picture that is well defined at any one moment is more contracted than it would be in a real scene; but, by moving the mental eye from point to point, the whole of the image, so far as it is remembered at all, may be successively brought into view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether mental images are spatially complete at once or built up by shifting attention; note whether subjects can bring the whole remembered scene into view by 'moving the mental eye.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility/control over mental images (manipulatability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Others have a complete mastery over their mental images. They can call up the figure of a friend, and make it sit on a chair or stand up at will; they can make it turn round and attitudinize in any way ... They are able to build up elaborate geometric structures bit by bit in their mind's eye, and add, subtract, or alter at will and at leisure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess subject's ability to manipulate, transform, and systematically alter mental images (pose, motion, assembly/disassembly) as a separate evaluative dimension; this skill is important for higher thought processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence/inflexibility of initial images (tenacity effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The persistency of the forms under which numerals and dates are visualized testifies to a want of flexibility in mental imagery which is characteristic of many persons. The first image they have acquired of any scene is apt to hold its place tenaciously in spite of subsequent need of correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tendency for first-acquired mental images to resist correction or reconfiguration; score inflexibility as a negative when flexibility is desired (e.g., accurate species or generic images).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of fixed associative phenomena (letter-color, number-forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are a few persons ... who cannot disentangle even the letters of the alphabet from the oddest associations with colors ... Another ... tendency is to visualize numerals in a peculiar manner ... they are never able to dissociate any single number from its own particular place in the field of their mental view ... the tendency to see them is strongly hereditary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and consider idiosyncratic persistent associations (synesthetic letter-color ties, fixed spatial number-forms, date-diagrams) as distinct characteristics; note their hereditability and utility (e.g., for simple mental arithmetic or mnemonics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic correlates: sex, age, education, heredity, race
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of visualizing is higher in the female sex than in the male, and is somewhat, but not much, higher in public-school boys than in men ... Language and book-learning certainly tend to dull it. The visualizing faculty is a natural gift ... has a tendency to be inherited. Since families differ so much ... races would also differ ... the French appear to possess the visualizing faculty in a high degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating imagery, consider demographic tendencies: females and some children score higher; education/literacy tends to reduce vividness; strong familial/hereditary patterns; possible cultural/racial differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppression of imagery as an index of abstract thought training
rubrics_metrics.description: A habit of suppressing mental imagery must, therefore, characterize men who deal much with abstract ideas; and, as the power of dealing easily and firmly with these ideas is the surest criterion of a high order of intellect, we should expect that the visualizing faculty would be starved by disuse among philosophers, and this is precisely what I have found on inquiry to be the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the ability or habit of suppressing specific mental imagery as indicative of abstract/analytic cognitive style; include suppression tendency as a factor when correlating imagery with intellectual type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for producing generalized (composite) images
rubrics_metrics.description: I proved two years ago that a generalized picture did as a matter of fact admit of being produced. I threw magic-lantern portraits of different persons on the top ... (Galton references: 'Composite Portraits', 'Generic Images').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use composite/overlay methods (e.g., overlaying portraits) to derive generalized or typical images from multiple exemplars; useful when seeking generic mental pictures for species/classes rather than particular exemplars.
